ConnectionGuide.Title: Would you like to set up connections?
ConnectionGuide.Intro: The Connection Service lets plugins connect to accounts you approve and can relay encrypted traffic between your phone and Headquarters. You can use Headquarters without it.
ConnectionGuide.HostedDetail: Connect to our public available service
ConnectionGuide.SelfDetail: Install the service on a machine you manage, or connect one you already run.
ConnectionGuide.LaterDetail: Finish setup now. You can return to Connections in Settings anytime.
ConnectionGuide.Where: Where will you run the service?
ConnectionGuide.LocationIntro: Choose where to install, or connect a service that is already running.
ConnectionGuide.LocalDetail: Install alongside Headquarters using Docker Compose.
ConnectionGuide.RemoteDetail: Take the setup file to the person or machine that will run it.
ConnectionGuide.ExistingDetail: Enter the HTTPS address supplied by the service owner.
ConnectionGuide.HostedIntro: Check the hosted service, then pair Headquarters to connect supported apps. You’ll approve account access when you set up a plugin.
ConnectionGuide.LocalIntro: On the Headquarters machine, install Docker with Compose 2.24 or later. Point a public DNS name at this machine and make ports 80 and 443 available for HTTPS setup.
ConnectionGuide.RemoteIntro: Choose a server with Docker and Compose 2.24 or later. Point a public DNS name at that server and make ports 80 and 443 available for HTTPS setup.
ConnectionGuide.Domain: Enter the HTTPS address people will use to reach this service.
ConnectionGuide.DomainRequired: Use a full DNS name on the standard HTTPS port, for example https://connections.example.com.
ConnectionGuide.Transfer: Send the file to the server administrator. In a folder containing the file on that server, run the command below. Docker builds the service and sets up HTTPS and persistent storage.
ConnectionGuide.Run: Save the file in its own folder on the Headquarters machine and run this command there. Docker builds the service and sets up HTTPS and persistent storage.
ConnectionGuide.AllowOrigin: Add the exact service address to the Headquarters API’s allowed origins. For a private network address, also add it to PrivateNetworkOrigins. Keep existing entries.
ConnectionGuide.PairSettings: Set the browser return address and two separate, protected absolute file paths for the deployment and owner keys. Restart the Headquarters API to apply these settings.
ConnectionGuide.OwnerApproval: Approve Headquarters on a service you own
ConnectionGuide.OwnerCommand: Prepare an owner bootstrap below and save the public request as owner.json. Review the permissions on the service host before running these commands there. Then check your permissions and approve the enrollment using the public pairing details above.
ConnectionGuide.PhoneService: On the service host, save phone.env beside compose.yaml and run docker compose up -d. For an existing service, merge these values into its configuration, keeping any other routes.
ConnectionGuide.PhoneHeadquarters: Set these values on the Headquarters API and restart it. Once its log reports an attached route, open Headquarters on your phone.
ConnectionGuide.LinkDisabled: Enable Installation:LinkingEnabled on the Headquarters API and restart it. Then link this workspace in Settings → C-Sweet account.
ConnectionGuide.LinkRequired: Link this Headquarters in Settings → C-Sweet account, then check phone setup again.
ConnectionGuide.HostedRoute: Ask your C-Sweet service administrator to provision a hosted phone route for this Headquarters and provide the relay origin and route ID.
ConnectionGuide.PhoneConfigured: Headquarters is configured to use the relay below. Open the mobile app to test the connection.
ConnectionGuide.PhoneRoute: This Headquarters needs a route on your service. The settings below contain its public routing keys.
ConnectionGuide.PhoneError: Couldn’t load phone setup. Check your account connection and try again.
